role_agent_name: Marine acoustics and hydrographic survey lead (ACOU)
abstract: Evaluates side-scan bathymetry sonar resolution and synthetic aperture tow-fish operational depth ratings
system_message:
You are Marine acoustics and hydrographic survey lead (ACOU). You serve as the Marine acoustics and hydrographic survey lead (ACOU), responsible for evaluating side-scan bathymetry sonar resolution and synthetic aperture tow-fish operational depth ratings, as well as reviewing sub-bottom magnetometer calibration metrics across candidate search plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Sub-bottom magnetometer calibration（MAGN）
information_points.content:
ACOU-MAGN-YWB：Regarding sub-bottom magnetometer calibration for the Oceanic Sentinel autonomous salvage taskforce, the geophysical sensor bench audit evaluated the towed marine magnetometer sensor pod at a magnetometer sampling sensitivity of 0.02 nT.
ACOU-MAGN-HU0：Regarding sub-bottom magnetometer calibration for the Benthic Explorer acoustic survey consortium, the towed marine magnetometer sensor pod demonstrated a magnetometer sampling sensitivity of 0.08 nT during the geophysical sensor bench audit.
ACOU-MAGN-HCF：Regarding sub-bottom magnetometer calibration for the Abyssal Surveyor deep-tow expedition, the geophysical sensor bench audit recorded a magnetometer sampling sensitivity of 0.05 nT for the towed marine magnetometer sensor pod.

information_points.title: Evaluates side-scan bathymetry sonar resolution and synthetic aperture tow-fish operational depth ratings（SONAR）
information_points.content:
ACOU-SONAR-2TR：For the Oceanic Sentinel autonomous salvage taskforce, the AUV acoustic across-track resolution resolved on the autonomous underwater vehicle payload is 0.1 m according to the hydrographic sensor verification trial. The vessel's equipment readiness manifest shows the tow-fish deployment system is enabled, and the pressure hull engineering certificate specifies a tow-fish rated operational depth of 5000 m.
ACOU-SONAR-MQK：For the Benthic Explorer acoustic survey consortium, the hydrographic sensor verification trial on the autonomous underwater vehicle payload established an AUV acoustic across-track resolution of 0.1 m. Furthermore, the mobilization equipment readiness manifest confirms that the tow-fish deployment system is enabled, and the pressure vessel engineering certificate reflects a tow-fish rated operational depth of 6000 m.
ACOU-SONAR-TBW：For the Abyssal Surveyor deep-tow expedition, the autonomous underwater vehicle payload demonstrates an AUV acoustic across-track resolution of 0.1 m based on the hydrographic sensor verification trial. In addition, the mission survey equipment manifest indicates the tow-fish deployment system is enabled, while the pressure vessel engineering certificate documents a tow-fish rated operational depth of 4000 m.
